source.primary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360). NB: Codex Vaticanus (B/03) DOES NOT contain Revelation — Revelation in Vaticanus has been LOST (the codex breaks off at Hebrews 9:14, and Revelation is not present); modern manuscripts of Vaticanus appended Revelation in late minuscule hands but this is not part of the original 4th-c. codex. For Revelation, Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Ephraemi Rescriptus + the early papyri are the primary witnesses.
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Alexandrinus (A/02; British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII, 5th c. CE) — for Revelation, Alexandrinus is in fact the SUPERIOR witness to Sinaiticus in many places, as Sinaiticus's Revelation text shows more scribal corruption than its Gospel-text. Modern editions weigh A more heavily for Revelation than for the rest of the NT. Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04; 5th c., palimpsest) also preserves much of Revelation.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P47 (Chester Beatty III; 3rd c. CE ~250) preserves Rev 9:10-17:2 — does NOT preserve Rev 1. P98 (P.IFAO inv. 237b; 2nd c. CE ~150) is the earliest Revelation papyrus — preserves Rev 1:13-2:1 fragmentarily; substantially confirms the consensus text for Rev 1:13-20. P115 (P.Oxy 4499; 3rd-4th c.) preserves portions of Rev 2-15. For Rev 1:1-12, the earliest preserved witnesses are the 4th-c. uncials (Sinaiticus) + 5th c. (Alexandrinus, Ephraemi).
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). For Revelation specifically: Hoskier *Concerning the Text of the Apocalypse* (Quaritch 1929) — the foundational critical-apparatus study. The Apocalypse has notoriously divergent textual streams (Andreas of Caesarea family, Koine family, Alexandrian family).
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Ephraemi + P98 (for vv.13-20) original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Hoskier 1929
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Hoskier 1929 for variants.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Hoskier, H. C., *Concerning the Text of the Apocalypse*, 2 vols. (Quaritch 1929). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg (4th c.). Codex Alexandrinus: British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII (5th c.). Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus: Bibliothèque nationale de France Gr. 9 (5th c., palimpsest). P47 = Chester Beatty III (3rd c.). P98 = P.IFAO inv. 237b (2nd c.). Aune WBC 1997-1998 (3-vol megacommentary); Beale NIGTC 1999; Charles ICC 1920; Koester AB 2014; Mounce NICNT 1997 rev.; Smalley *The Revelation to John* (IVP 2005); Bauckham *The Climax of Prophecy* (T&T Clark 1993); Collins *Crisis and Catharsis* (Westminster 1984); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The Revelation text is notoriously the most-textually-uncertain book of the NT (less papyrus support than Gospels/Paul; smaller pool of mss). The Greek of Revelation is famously irregular — full of solecisms, Hebraisms, and grammatical anomalies that make the author's Greek-as-second-language status visible (Charles ICC 1.cxvii-clix is the classic analysis). The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated.

verses.text: Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεός, δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει, καὶ ἐσήμανεν ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννῃ,
verses.translit: Apokalypsis Iēsou Christou, hēn edōken autō ho theos, deixai tois doulois autou ha dei genesthai en tachei, kai esēmanen aposteilas dia tou angelou autou tō doulō autou Iōannē,
verses.notes: **OPENING — TITLE-INCIPIT**. *Apokalypsis* (unveiling / revelation) — gives the book its name; first word. *ha dei genesthai en tachei* (what must happen soon) — eschatological-imminence formula echoing Dan 2:28 LXX (*ha dei genesthai ep’ eschatōn tōn hēmerōn*). The Lukan-equivalent is in Mark 13 / Luke 21 / Matt 24. **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: *apokalypsis* + *deixai* (show) + revelation-through-angel-to-John frame is the densest single-verse engagement-site in the Raëlian canon (Raël's own claimed-revelation narrative explicitly mirrors this verse's structure: shown what-must-happen via messenger-encounter). Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE.**

verses.text: ὃς ἐμαρτύρησεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅσα εἶδεν.
verses.translit: hos emartyrēsen ton logon tou theou kai tēn martyrian Iēsou Christou, hosa eiden.
verses.notes: John as witness-attestor. *hosa eiden* (whatsoever he saw) — the visionary-witness frame (cf. v.11, 19; 4:1).

verses.text: μακάριος ὁ ἀναγινώσκων καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας καὶ τηροῦντες τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ γεγραμμένα, ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς ἐγγύς.
verses.translit: makarios ho anaginōskōn kai hoi akountes tous logous tēs prophēteias kai tērountes ta en autē gegrammena, ho gar kairos engys.
verses.notes: **FIRST BEATITUDE OF REVELATION** (the book has seven; this is #1). *anaginōskōn* (the reader [aloud]) + *akountes* (the hearers) — liturgical-reading setting (cf. Col 4:16). *ho kairos engys* (the time is near) — imminence formula.

verses.text: Ἰωάννης ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις ταῖς ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἑπτὰ πνευμάτων ἃ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Iōannēs tais hepta ekklēsiais tais en tē Asia· charis hymin kai eirēnē apo ho ōn kai ho ēn kai ho erchomenos, kai apo tōn hepta pneumatōn ha enōpion tou thronou autou,
verses.notes: **LETTER-PRESCRIPT TO SEVEN CHURCHES**. *hai hepta ekklēsiai* — the seven churches of Asia (named at v.11): Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea. **MAJOR GRAMMATICAL SOLECISM**: *apo ho ōn kai ho ēn kai ho erchomenos* — *apo* normally takes the genitive, but the author keeps the nominative articles ("from THE-ONE-WHO-IS"), treating the divine-formula as an indeclinable name. This is a deliberate grammatical-shocker preserving the Greek-Septuagintal divine-name-by-circumlocution (cf. Exod 3:14 LXX *egō eimi ho ōn*). *ho ōn kai ho ēn kai ho erchomenos* (the one who is and the one who was and the one who is coming) — Hebrew tetragrammaton-equivalent. *tōn hepta pneumatōn* (the seven spirits) — likely cross-corpus to Isa 11:2 LXX (the seven Spirit-gifts on the Branch); cf. Zech 4:2; 4:10; Rev 4:5; 5:6. Aune WBC 1.31-34.

verses.text: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστός, ὁ πρωτότοκος τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ὁ ἄρχων τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς. Τῷ ἀγαπῶντι ἡμᾶς καὶ λύσαντι ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: kai apo Iēsou Christou, ho martys ho pistos, ho prōtotokos tōn nekrōn kai ho archōn tōn basileōn tēs gēs. Tō agapōnti hēmas kai lysanti hēmas ek tōn hamartiōn hēmōn en tō aimati autou,
verses.notes: Christological triad: faithful witness + firstborn of the dead + ruler of earthly kings. Cross-corpus Ps 89:27 (88:28 LXX) *kagō prōtotokon thēsomai auton, hypsēlon para tois basileusin tēs gēs*. Variant: *lysanti* (loosed) vs. *lousanti* (washed) — minimal pair distinguished by accent only in unaccented uncials. NA28/SBLGNT read *lysanti* (Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus); some Byzantine + KJV-tradition read *lousanti* ("washed us in his blood"). The *en tō aimati* + *lysanti* is the harder reading.

verses.text: καὶ ἐποίησεν ἡμᾶς βασιλείαν, ἱερεῖς τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ — αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
verses.translit: kai epoiēsen hēmas basileian, hiereis tō theō kai patri autou — autō hē doxa kai to kratos eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn· amēn.
verses.notes: **KINGDOM-OF-PRIESTS FORMULA**. *epoiēsen hēmas basileian, hiereis* (made us a kingdom, priests) — cross-corpus **Exod 19:6** LXX *basileion hierateuma* (royal priesthood); cf. 1 Pet 2:9. Revelation's recurring kingdom-priesthood theme (cf. 5:10; 20:6). Doxology + amēn.

verses.text: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν, καὶ ὄψεται αὐτὸν πᾶς ὀφθαλμὸς καὶ οἵτινες αὐτὸν ἐξεκέντησαν, καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς. ναί, ἀμήν.
verses.translit: Idou erchetai meta tōn nephelōn, kai opsetai auton pas ophthalmos kai hoitines auton exekentēsan, kai kopsontai ep’ auton pasai hai phylai tēs gēs. nai, amēn.
verses.notes: **MAJOR DANIELIC + ZECHARIAH CROSS-CORPUS**. *erchetai meta tōn nephelōn* (he is coming with the clouds) — direct cross-corpus **Dan 7:13 LXX/Th** (*hōs huios anthrōpou ērcheto kai … meta tōn nephelōn tou ouranou*). *hoitines auton exekentēsan* (those who pierced him) + *kopsontai* (will mourn) — cross-corpus **Zech 12:10** LXX (Hebrew *daqaru*, 'pierced'); cf. John 19:37. A conflated-citation. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: *erchetai meta tōn nephelōn* (coming with the clouds) is one of the most-heavily-engaged verses in the Raëlian canon — read as the Elohim returning with their craft. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE** toward (a) conventional parousia theology, (b) preterist 70-CE fulfillment reading, or (c) Raëlian craft-return reading.

verses.text: Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, λέγει κύριος ὁ θεός, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, ὁ παντοκράτωρ.
verses.translit: Egō eimi to Alpha kai to Ō, legei kyrios ho theos, ho ōn kai ho ēn kai ho erchomenos, ho pantokratōr.
verses.notes: **ALPHA AND OMEGA**. *to Alpha kai to Ō* — first and last letters of the Greek alphabet = totality/eternity epithet. Cross-corpus 21:6; 22:13. *pantokratōr* (almighty / all-ruler) — LXX rendering of Hebrew *Sabaoth* (hosts) and *Shaddai*. Major Apocalyptic divine epithet.

verses.text: Ἐγὼ Ἰωάννης, ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὑμῶν καὶ συγκοινωνὸς ἐν τῇ θλίψει καὶ βασιλείᾳ καὶ ὑπομονῇ ἐν Ἰησοῦ, ἐγενόμην ἐν τῇ νήσῳ τῇ καλουμένῃ Πάτμῳ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: Egō Iōannēs, ho adelphos hymōn kai synkoinōnos en tē thlipsei kai basileia kai hypomonē en Iēsou, egenomēn en tē nēsō tē kaloumenē Patmō dia ton logon tou theou kai tēn martyrian Iēsou.
verses.notes: **PATMOS SETTING**. John on **Patmos** — small island in the Dodecanese (Aegean), ~60 km off the coast of Asia Minor (Miletus). Roman penal-exile-island. Pliny *NH* 4.69 + Tacitus *Ann.* 4.30 confirm Patmos as exile-location. The exile is variously dated to Nero (mid-60s — minority view) or Domitian (mid-90s — majority view, after Irenaeus *Adv. Haer.* 5.30.3).

verses.text: ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι ἐν τῇ κυριακῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ ἤκουσα ὀπίσω μου φωνὴν μεγάλην ὡς σάλπιγγος
verses.translit: egenomēn en pneumati en tē kyriakē hēmera, kai ēkousa opisō mou phōnēn megalēn hōs salpingos
verses.notes: **ECSTATIC-TRANCE FORMULA**. *egenomēn en pneumati* (I came-to-be in spirit) — Lukan-Pauline ecstatic-state vocabulary (cf. 4:2). *en tē kyriakē hēmera* (on the Lord's day) — EARLIEST KNOWN ATTESTATION of *kyriakē* as designation for Sunday/the Christian weekly liturgical day (cf. Didache 14:1). *phōnēn megalēn hōs salpingos* (loud voice like a trumpet) — cross-corpus Exod 19:16, 19; 20:18 (Sinai theophany-trumpet); Heb 12:19. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: *en pneumati* trance-state engaged in Raëlian and other heterodox readings as altered-state / contact-state; preserve.

verses.text: λεγούσης· Ὃ βλέπεις γράψον εἰς βιβλίον καὶ πέμψον ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις, εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εἰς Σμύρναν καὶ εἰς Πέργαμον καὶ εἰς Θυάτειρα καὶ εἰς Σάρδεις καὶ εἰς Φιλαδέλφειαν καὶ εἰς Λαοδίκειαν.
verses.translit: legousēs· Ho blepeis grapson eis biblion kai pempson tais hepta ekklēsiais, eis Epheson kai eis Smyrnan kai eis Pergamon kai eis Thyateira kai eis Sardeis kai eis Philadelpheian kai eis Laodikeian.
verses.notes: **SEVEN-CHURCHES LIST**. The seven cities are listed in clockwise geographical order along a Roman postal-route through western Asia Minor (Hemer *The Letters to the Seven Churches* 1986).

verses.text: καὶ ἐπέστρεψα βλέπειν τὴν φωνὴν ἥτις ἐλάλει μετ’ ἐμοῦ· καὶ ἐπιστρέψας εἶδον ἑπτὰ λυχνίας χρυσᾶς,
verses.translit: kai epestrepsa blepein tēn phōnēn hētis elalei met’ emou· kai epistrepsas eidon hepta lychnias chrysas,
verses.notes: **SEVEN GOLDEN LAMPSTANDS**. Cross-corpus Zech 4:2 (the seven-branched lampstand vision) + Exod 25:31-40 (the Tabernacle menorah). The lampstand-image will be interpreted in v.20.

verses.text: καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν λυχνιῶν ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἐνδεδυμένον ποδήρη καὶ περιεζωσμένον πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς ζώνην χρυσᾶν·
verses.translit: kai en mesō tōn lychniōn homoion huion anthrōpou, endedymenon podērē kai periezōsmenon pros tois mastois zōnēn chrysan·
verses.notes: **MAJOR DANIEL CROSS-CORPUS — SON OF MAN AMONG THE LAMPSTANDS**. *homoion huion anthrōpou* (one like a son of man) — direct cross-corpus **Dan 7:13** LXX/Th (*hōs huios anthrōpou*). *podērē* (long robe — the high-priestly garment) — cross-corpus LXX Exod 28:4, 27; Ezek 9:2-3, 11; Wis 18:24 (associating *podērēs* with cosmic-priestly status). *periezōsmenon pros tois mastois zōnēn chrysan* (girded across the chest with a golden sash) — cross-corpus Dan 10:5 LXX (*periezōsmenos en linō, kai hē osphys autou periezōsmenē en chrysiō*). This verse is preserved in P98 (2nd c. CE) — earliest external witness. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: the *huios anthrōpou* in shining-robe + golden-girdle vision is intensely engaged in heterodox + Raëlian readings as humanoid-figure-encounter; preserve the throne-vision tradition. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE.**

verses.text: ἡ δὲ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ αἱ τρίχες λευκαὶ ὡς ἔριον λευκόν, ὡς χιών, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς φλὸξ πυρός,
verses.translit: hē de kephalē autou kai hai triches leukai hōs erion leukon, hōs chiōn, kai hoi ophthalmoi autou hōs phlox pyros,
verses.notes: **MAJOR DANIEL CROSS-CORPUS — ANCIENT-OF-DAYS ATTRIBUTES TRANSFERRED TO SON-OF-MAN**. *hē kephalē … hai triches leukai hōs erion leukon, hōs chiōn* — direct cross-corpus **Dan 7:9** LXX (the Ancient of Days: *to triche tēs kephalēs autou hōsei erion katharon*). Theologically significant: attributes of the Ancient of Days are here transferred to the *huios anthrōpou*. *hoi ophthalmoi … hōs phlox pyros* (eyes like a flame of fire) — cross-corpus Dan 10:6 LXX. Composite-Danielic theophany.

verses.text: καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ ὡς ἐν καμίνῳ πεπυρωμένης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ αὐτοῦ ὡς φωνὴ ὑδάτων πολλῶν,
verses.translit: kai hoi podes autou homoioi chalkolibanō hōs en kaminō pepyrōmenēs, kai hē phōnē autou hōs phōnē hydatōn pollōn,
verses.notes: *chalkolibanō* (chalcolibanus / bronze-frankincense) — hapax in NT (only here + 2:18); identity uncertain (possibly an electrum-bronze alloy or polished brass). *hōs phōnē hydatōn pollōn* (like the sound of many waters) — cross-corpus **Ezek 1:24** LXX (the chayyot wing-sound); Ezek 43:2 LXX (kavod-arrival). Major Ezekielian throne-vision echo.

verses.text: καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρας ἑπτά, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ῥομφαία δίστομος ὀξεῖα ἐκπορευομένη, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος φαίνει ἐν τῇ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai echōn en tē dexia cheiri autou asteras hepta, kai ek tou stomatos autou rhomphaia distomos oxeia ekporeuomenē, kai hē opsis autou hōs ho hēlios phainei en tē dynamei autou.
verses.notes: **MULTIPLE COMPOSITE-IMAGERY**. (a) seven stars in right hand — interpreted as the angels of the seven churches (v.20). (b) *rhomphaia distomos oxeia* (sharp two-edged sword) from the mouth — cross-corpus Isa 49:2 (*ethēken to stoma mou hōsei machairan oxeian*); Heb 4:12; Wis 18:16; cf. Rev 19:15. (c) *hē opsis autou hōs ho hēlios* (face like the sun) — cross-corpus Judg 5:31 LXX; Matt 17:2 (transfiguration *to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios*); Dan 10:6 LXX (*to prosōpon autou hōsei horasis astrapēs*). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: solar-face + sword-from-mouth imagery preserved at surface; heterodox decodings (including Raëlian) deflect to the apparatus.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδον αὐτόν, ἔπεσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὡς νεκρός· καὶ ἔθηκεν τὴν δεξιὰν αὐτοῦ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος,
verses.translit: Kai hote eidon auton, epesa pros tous podas autou hōs nekros· kai ethēken tēn dexian autou ep’ eme legōn· Mē phobou· egō eimi ho prōtos kai ho eschatos,
verses.notes: **PROSTRATION-RESPONSE + DIVINE SELF-PREDICATION**. *epesa … hōs nekros* (fell as dead) — cross-corpus Dan 8:18; 10:8-10 (Daniel's collapses before angelic-vision); Ezek 1:28. *Mē phobou* (do not fear) — angelophany formula. *egō eimi ho prōtos kai ho eschatos* (I am the first and the last) — direct cross-corpus **Isa 41:4, 44:6, 48:12** (the divine self-predication 'I am he, I am the first and the last'). Theologically significant: divine self-predication-formula applied to the *huios anthrōpou* figure.

verses.text: καὶ ὁ ζῶν, καὶ ἐγενόμην νεκρὸς καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶν εἰμι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ ἔχω τὰς κλεῖς τοῦ θανάτου καὶ τοῦ ᾅδου.
verses.translit: kai ho zōn, kai egenomēn nekros kai idou zōn eimi eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, kai echō tas kleis tou thanatou kai tou hadou.
verses.notes: **RESURRECTION-CLAIM + KEYS OF DEATH AND HADES**. *tas kleis tou thanatou kai tou hadou* (the keys of death and Hades) — cross-corpus Isa 22:22 (key-of-David); the post-resurrection harrowing-of-Hades tradition (1 Pet 3:18-22). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of the resurrection.

verses.text: γράψον οὖν ἃ εἶδες καὶ ἃ εἰσὶν καὶ ἃ μέλλει γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.
verses.translit: grapson oun ha eides kai ha eisin kai ha mellei genesthai meta tauta.
verses.notes: **TRIPLE-WRITING COMMAND** — past/present/future: "what you have seen, what is, what is to take place after these things." Variously read as the book's structural-program. Aune WBC 1.105 surveys options.

verses.text: τὸ μυστήριον τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀστέρων οὓς εἶδες ἐπὶ τῆς δεξιᾶς μου, καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ λυχνίας τὰς χρυσᾶς· οἱ ἑπτὰ ἀστέρες ἄγγελοι τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ αἱ λυχνίαι αἱ ἑπτὰ ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαι εἰσίν.
verses.translit: to mystērion tōn hepta asterōn hous eides epi tēs dexias mou, kai tas hepta lychnias tas chrysas· hoi hepta asteres angeloi tōn hepta ekklēsiōn eisin, kai hai lychniai hai hepta hepta ekklēsiai eisin.
verses.notes: **INTERPRETATION-FORMULA — REVELATION'S APOCALYPTIC HERMENEUTIC**. *to mystērion* (the mystery) + identification-key: stars = *angeloi* of the churches; lampstands = the churches themselves. *angeloi tōn ekklēsiōn* — interpretation debated: (a) heavenly-patron angels of each congregation; (b) human-messengers (bishops?); (c) the prevailing-spirit / character of each church. Cross-corpus Dan 10:13, 20-21 (national-patron angels — Michael for Israel, prince of Persia, prince of Greece). Aune WBC 1.108-112.
